manualApplyStatus: authored - manual apply pending (CP-051). NOT applied to any environment, hosted or local. No reset, no --include-all, no forced or full-chain replay. The backfill in section 9 DOES write rows on apply - it is additive, idempotent, and writes only into the two NEW reconciliation tables, never into a pre-existing table.
whatThisFileDoes: CP-095's append-only manager-controlled operational status ledger, and CP-096's explicit link/reconciliation rows in the `venue_identity_bridges` shape. It creates the substrate legacy workforce records are reconciled INTO, seeds that substrate from provable sources only, and does NOT create a single department or membership.

representativeSnapshot.kind: Static review plus EXECUTED behavioural evidence on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster with the chain's own authority loaded by line range. Four results are measurements rather than readings. (1) THE LEDGER'S APPEND-ONLY PROPERTY IS ATTACKED THREE WAYS: as the table owner under FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, as service_role which has BYPASSRLS, and as service_role with the UPDATE privilege RESTORED BY HAND. All three are refused, by three different mechanisms - the trigger, the revoked grant, and the trigger again - so removing any one still leaves the history unrewritable. The original event still reads 'working' after four attempts. (2) THE BACKFILL IS MEASURED NOT TO REPLACE: re-applying over two free-text department strings, one org-less staff row, one name-only vendor contract, one name-only event request, one tour-scoped vendor and one tenant-less staffing agency created ZERO departments and ZERO memberships, and produced 14 reviewable link rows and 13 quarantine rows; a third apply left both counts unchanged. (3) A DEPARTMENT WITH OPERATIONAL HISTORY CANNOT BE DELETED: the DELETE is refused 23503, so CP-095's 'corrections append superseding events' is not defeatable by a cascade. (4) THE QUARANTINE VISIBILITY SPLIT: an org administrator sees 2 of the 14 link rows, because the rows whose subject has no established organization are invisible to every authenticated caller and reachable only as service_role.
representativeSnapshot.evidenceArtifact: executed:supabase/tests/wfc004_workforce_departments.harness.sh ALL CHECKS PASSED, 156 PASS / 0 FAIL, exit 0, PostgreSQL 16.15 throwaway cluster (migration SHA-256 0151210fdc0626c07997b14692357e915302fb781928914594234fc3db7d734e). Stages 3i, 3j and 4 of that harness are this file's evidence.

assumptions: CP-095 IS ENFORCED BY THREE INDEPENDENT MECHANISMS, so none of them alone has to be trusted. (1) NO UPDATE OR DELETE PRIVILEGE: the grant block is `revoke all` from anon, authenticated AND service_role followed by `grant select, insert` - a reset and a narrow grant, not a list of targeted revokes, because an EXPLICIT grant does not remove a privilege a default-privileges sweep already granted, so the only complete way to say 'append-only for every role that is not the table owner' is to reset the privilege set. service_role is included on purpose: it has BYPASSRLS, so a POLICY is not a control against it, and a default-privileges grant to service_role is the realistic way this history would be re-opened in a year. (2) AN IMMUTABILITY TRIGGER on UPDATE and DELETE that RAISEs, SECURITY INVOKER, so it applies to the owner and to service_role alike and only a genuine superuser could bypass it - and that is the platform, not a code path. (3) `public.workforce_operational_status_current`, a security_invoker view that derives the current value, because an append-only history is only useful if a reader can derive the present from it and putting that derivation in the database means the 'current' answer cannot drift from the ledger. MEASURED: removing any one of the three still leaves the history unrewritable.

CP-095'S REQUIRED FIELDS, ALL ENFORCED: actor (`recorded_by uuid not null`, plus a trigger that requires it to equal auth.uid() whenever a JWT is present - MEASURED, a forged actor is refused); effective time (`effective_at`, deliberately SEPARATE from `recorded_at` so a retroactive change is visible as such); source (`source` constrained to manager | system | import); and a REQUIRED REASON for exceptional or retroactive changes, enforced by a ROW-LOCAL CHECK so an application that forgot to validate still cannot write it. The reason rule's exact shape was CORRECTED BY EXECUTION: the first revision treated `released` as exceptional, and the harness refused an ordinary present-tense `released` with no reason - which was the CONSTRAINT being wrong, not the write, because requiring a reason for every shift's end would train managers to write 'done' fifty times a night. The exceptional set is now exactly `absent` and `excused`, the two statuses that remove a person from being expected, and both are measured.

WORKER EVIDENCE IS STRUCTURALLY SEPARATE, AND THE SEPARATION IS A GRANT AND A POLICY, NOT A CONVENTION. Check-ins, responses and acknowledgements already live in the `work_mode_*` relations DB-010 created (20260922155356) and this migration neither reads nor writes them. The ledger's INSERT policy admits department-management authority AND workforce.view on the row's organization - there is NO arm a worker-only path can satisfy, so a worker cannot write a manager state event at all, and 'worker evidence never silently overwrites manager state' is therefore true because the overwrite is not writable. The `workforce.view` conjunct is not generosity and is load-bearing: DB-016 withholds workforce.manage from department_manager (WFC-003 §2.5.2), so without it a department manager could WRITE presence and never READ it back, which is CP-110's plausible zero arriving through authorization.

CP-096: RECONCILE, DO NOT REPLACE, AND THE BACKFILL HAS NO PROVABLE SOURCE TO WORK FROM - which is a finding, not caution. There is NO provable source for a workforce membership. The only department-bearing column in the chain is `staff_members.department`, an unconstrained nullable TEXT column with no foreign key and no department table anywhere (WFC-003 §5 item 8), and WFC-003 §6.9 requires the department entity to replace every free-text department column BY EXPLICIT LINK, NEVER BY VALUE COMPARISON. Creating a department named after a free-text string and attaching people to it by matching that string is exactly the value comparison CP-096 forbids and the resolution that would manufacture the authority the new schema exists to stop inventing. So every one of those strings becomes a QUARANTINE ROW with its row count and its organizations recorded - reviewable, countable, and not an authority input. A user's `org_members` membership is NOT accepted as a provable source for a `staff_members.org_id` anywhere in this file (WFC-003 §1.2c, ambiguity 23); the provable sources are exactly the two 20260821031214:10-28 used, entity_type='org' with the id present in organizations and entity_type='event' with events_v2.org_id non-null.

EVERY BACKFILL IS IDEMPOTENT BY CONSTRUCTION, and this is MEASURED rather than asserted: a unique key on the subject, `on conflict ... do update ... where` an `is distinct from` guard, so a second run writes nothing and a CHANGED classification is recorded rather than duplicated. The harness applies this file three times over the same legacy rows and the link and quarantine counts are identical after the second and third. The six chain-absent reader relations are seeded with `on conflict do nothing` because their classification cannot change without this file changing.

NO AUTOMATIC MERGE, EVER. `vendor_contracts`, `event_vendor_requests`, `tour_vendors` and `staffing_agencies` are recorded as `vendor_identity_name_only` with the reason in the evidence payload, because a name cannot be shown to be the same company across two rows and therefore cannot own a workforce department (WFC-003 §3.2). staffing_agencies is a vendor-company-adjacent table with NO tenant column at all and is explicitly NOT adopted - WFC-003 §5 item 14 asks whether these are vendors and this file answers by quarantining, not by merging. The evidence records that `vendor_contracts.status` is contract lifecycle and `event_vendor_requests.status` is request lifecycle, neither of which is the vendor-master vocabulary, so a reviewer can see that three incompatible status vocabularies exist rather than being handed a merge.

THE SIX CHAIN-ABSENT READER RELATIONS ARE RECORDED AS TABLE-LEVEL OBSERVATIONS WITH THEIR READER SITES AS EVIDENCE, because 'this table is missing' is only actionable next to 'these are the places that read it and what each renders when it is absent' (WFC-003 §3.3.2). The evidence payload for `vendors` records the executed 42703 argument; for `org_vendors` it records that the merge question is UNRESOLVED and what a single catalog query would settle it; for `vendor_compliance_documents` it records that it is the SAME ENTITY as archived `vendor_documents` under different column names; for `org_contracts` and `contract_signature_envelopes` it records that these are a CONTRACT-LIFECYCLE surface with no DDL and no ADR anywhere, so they need a product owner and a column contract rather than a database decision; and for `vendor_aliases` it records the silent data loss in `planVendorMerge` and the canonical home this programme provides.

`org_id` IS NULLABLE HERE, DELIBERATELY, and it is the only nullable tenant key in this wave. staffing_agencies has no tenant column at all, so a quarantine row about it cannot name one; `tour_vendors` has none either. Under the RLS policies such a row is invisible to every authenticated caller, because NULL never satisfies `has_perm`, which is the correct outcome and not a bug: an observation with no established organization is exactly the `org_key_missing` case and a platform operator is who resolves it. MEASURED: an org administrator sees 2 of 14 link rows. Every other WFC-004 relation carries `organizations.id` NOT NULL per WFC-003 §6.1; this one is a record ABOUT a subject, not a tenant-scoped resource.

THE QUARANTINE VOCABULARY IS WFC-003'S, TRANSCRIBED, ALL ELEVEN, and asserted by count and by the chain-anchored cross-check. A quarantine vocabulary that drifts from the contract's is a second, incompatible notion of 'unresolved', which is the CP-102 failure shape applied to a code list. `node supabase/tests/wfc004_guarded_block_order.mjs --exemptions`-style chain anchoring is the discipline applied to CP-107's exemption list; here the list is small and static, and the harness asserts the two tables agree on it and that every seeded row's code is in it.

THE LEDGER REFERENCES ITS DEPARTMENT WITH `on delete restrict` WHILE THE MANAGER AND MEMBERSHIP RELATIONS CASCADE - and the asymmetry IS the point. A department that has operational history cannot be deleted, only deactivated, so CP-095's 'corrections append superseding events' is not defeated by a cascade. MEASURED: the DELETE is refused 23503. Deleting a department still cascades its manager and membership rows, which is acceptable because those rows carry their own retirement columns and because the delete is an organization-administrator action on a workforce.manage policy. Stated rather than presented as uniform.

NO `information_schema.tables` EXISTENCE GUARD APPEARS IN THIS FILE, and that is ASSERTED rather than assumed: all five reconciliation sources (staff_members 20250818120000:211, vendor_contracts 20260825131000:48, event_vendor_requests 20260328150000:6, tour_vendors 20250818121000:51, staffing_agencies 20250812090500:20) are created by EARLIER version numbers, the post-condition checks all five with to_regclass, and the backfill itself read them - so a missing one would have aborted the transaction. `node supabase/tests/wfc004_guarded_block_order.mjs` measures that absence against the real 315-migration chain, and its self-test proves the instrument can fail.

Every pre-existing row is preserved. No pre-existing relation is created, altered or dropped; no pre-existing column is touched; no pre-existing data row is read for update or deleted. The backfill INSERTS into two new tables and UPDATES only rows in one of them, under an `is distinct from` guard. The `grant all ... to service_role` for the two reconciliation tables is deliberate - a platform operator needs to resolve quarantines - and DELETE is still reset away for every role including service_role, because a resolved quarantine is the record that it was examined.

lib/database.types.ts is byte-unchanged and this migration DOES require a type regeneration: it creates three tables, two views and two trigger functions that the contract does not declare. Regeneration is blocked (CP-089, CP-092) and is not attempted. The exact specification of what regeneration must produce is in this manifest and in the task record.
layeredPlan: Layer 0 (preflight, read-only, operator). Run the Layer 0 queries and record every result. Five things decide whether this file is correct for THIS target: (a) the ROW COUNTS of the five reconciliation sources and, specifically, `count(*) FILTER (WHERE department IS NOT NULL AND btrim(department) <> '')` and `count(DISTINCT btrim(department))` on staff_members - the backfill creates one quarantine row per distinct value, so a target with 40,000 distinct department strings creates 40,000 rows in each of two tables, and the operator should be able to say out loud whether that is acceptable for this target. (b) `count(*) FILTER (WHERE org_id IS NULL)` on staff_members - one quarantine row each. (c) `count(*)` on vendor_contracts, event_vendor_requests, tour_vendors and staffing_agencies. (d) the two grant preconditions: `has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.organizations','select')` and `has_schema_privilege('authenticated','auth','usage')`. (e) `to_regclass` of the five sources - the post-condition checks them, but knowing before the apply whether they are present is what distinguishes 'the apply failed' from 'the target is not what the file was written against'.

Layer 1 (apply, single run, operator). One transaction, explicit, this file only - never `supabase db reset`, never `db push --include-all`, never a chain replay (CP-051). Three CREATE TABLE, indexes, RLS enable+force on all three, nine DROP+CREATE POLICY, two CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER FUNCTION, two CREATE TRIGGER each preceded by DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS, the `revoke all` + narrow `grant` block, two CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW with (security_invoker = true), the eleven backfill statements, and a DO block that RAISEs unless: all three relations exist with RLS enabled AND forced; the ledger holds no update/delete privilege for anon, authenticated OR service_role; both ledger triggers are present; both views are security_invoker; all five reconciliation sources exist AT THIS VERSION POSITION; at least 6 link rows exist (the six chain-absent reader tables are seeded unconditionally, so 6 is the floor on an empty database); exactly 6 vendor_table_unproven quarantine rows exist; every link row agrees with its own quarantine code; and no policy on any of the three carries an unconditional clause or is anon/PUBLIC-reachable. The post-condition is inside the same transaction, so a target that cannot reach the asserted state fails the apply. A CORRECT RESULT INCLUDES a failed apply from the source-existence assertion, which means one of the five reconciliation sources is absent and the file must not be applied until that is understood.

Layer 2 (postflight, read-only, operator). Run `psql -f supabase/tests/wfc004_workforce_departments_contract.sql`; expect ZERO violation rows and one summary row `WFC-004 workforce departments|t|0`. Then the labelled probes. WHAT A CORRECT RESULT LOOKS LIKE, including the results that are correct and must not be 'fixed': the org administrator seeing FEWER reconciliation rows than exist is CORRECT, because org-less observations are invisible by design; zero vendor_table_unproven rows beyond the six is CORRECT because the source tables do not exist; and a department with status history refusing DELETE is CORRECT. WHAT IS NOT CORRECT: any UPDATE or DELETE privilege appearing on the ledger for any of the three roles, a policy on the ledger with no INSERT or SELECT arm, or a reconciliation row whose link_state and quarantine_code disagree.

Layer 3 (no fourth layer in this lane). Eight items are ROUTED: the vendors/org_vendors merge and the two contract-lifecycle relations' missing column contract (the vendor-domain owner, via HF-DB-012-VENDOR-ENTITY-MERGE-UNRESOLVED); whether the vendor.* permissions are provisioned in org_role_permissions (WFC-003 under CP-102 - this file does NOT widen the matrix, because any matrix write invalidates every active acting-context session); the affected-row-count requirement on every write command (WFC-005); whether `is_org_member` should be enforced at the seven live read sites that do not filter on status (WORK-102); the parity surface of the seven live `app/api/admin/workforce/**` routes (WFC-005/WFC-006); the 'at least one active primary membership' lifecycle rule (WFC-005's command layer, detected here by workforce_membership_health); attendance reconciliation between this ledger and the work_mode_* evidence layer (WFC-019); and whether org_members.revoked_at should be maintained alongside status (WFC-003 ambiguity 6, which mandates status and only status).

rowCountQueries: SELECT count(*) AS staff_members_rows, count(*) FILTER (WHERE org_id IS NULL) AS staff_rows_without_org, count(*) FILTER (WHERE department IS NOT NULL AND btrim(department) <> '') AS staff_rows_with_free_text_department, count(DISTINCT btrim(department)) FILTER (WHERE department IS NOT NULL AND btrim(department) <> '') AS distinct_free_text_department_values FROM public.staff_members
SELECT count(*) AS vendor_contracts_rows, count(DISTINCT btrim(vendor_name)) AS distinct_vendor_names FROM public.vendor_contracts WHERE vendor_name IS NOT NULL AND btrim(vendor_name) <> ''
SELECT count(*) AS event_vendor_request_rows FROM public.event_vendor_requests
SELECT count(*) AS tour_vendors_rows FROM public.tour_vendors
SELECT count(*) AS staffing_agencies_rows FROM public.staffing_agencies

SELECT to_regclass('public.staff_members') AS staff_members_exists, to_regclass('public.vendor_contracts') AS vendor_contracts_exists, to_regclass('public.event_vendor_requests') AS event_vendor_requests_exists, to_regclass('public.tour_vendors') AS tour_vendors_exists, to_regclass('public.staffing_agencies') AS staffing_agencies_exists

SELECT r.rolname, has_table_privilege(r.rolname,'public.workforce_operational_status_events','select') AS sel, has_table_privilege(r.rolname,'public.workforce_operational_status_events','insert') AS ins, has_table_privilege(r.rolname,'public.workforce_operational_status_events','update') AS upd, has_table_privilege(r.rolname,'public.workforce_operational_status_events','delete') AS del, has_table_privilege(r.rolname,'public.workforce_operational_status_events','truncate') AS trunc FROM pg_roles r WHERE r.rolname IN ('anon','authenticated','service_role') ORDER BY r.rolname
SELECT count(*) AS existing_workforce_legacy_links FROM public.workforce_legacy_links
SELECT count(*) AS departments_with_history FROM public.workforce_departments d WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.workforce_operational_status_events e WHERE e.department_id = d.id)

SELECT n.nspname, c.relname, c.relkind FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE c.relname IN ('vendors','org_vendors','vendor_compliance_documents','org_contracts','contract_signature_envelopes','vendor_aliases') ORDER BY 1,2
preflight.expectedAffectedRows: This is the ONE WFC-004 migration that writes rows on apply, and every row goes into a NEW table. Expected inserts into public.workforce_legacy_links: one row per distinct non-empty trimmed staff_members.department value; one per vendor_contracts row with a non-empty vendor_name; one per event_vendor_requests row likewise; one per tour_vendors row likewise; one per staffing_agencies row with a non-empty name; one per staff_members row with org_id IS NULL; and exactly 6 table-level rows for the chain-absent reader relations. Expected inserts into public.workforce_quarantine: the same set, keyed by (subject_table, code, coalesce(subject_id, subject_key)). Every ON CONFLICT branch is guarded by `is distinct from` or `resolved_at is null`, so a second apply writes nothing. ZERO rows in any pre-existing table are updated or deleted, and ZERO rows are created in public.workforce_departments, public.workforce_department_managers or public.workforce_department_memberships - MEASURED by the harness, not asserted. THE OPERATOR MUST SIZE THE FIRST RUN: a target with 40,000 distinct free-text department values creates 40,000 link rows and 40,000 quarantine rows, in one transaction.

execution.resumeStrategy: Authored - manual apply pending (CP-051). One transaction, one file. The three CREATE TABLE take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks only on relations that do not yet exist. The indexes are on new tables. The backfill READS five pre-existing tables and INSERTS into two new ones, so it adds no lock to any existing table beyond the ACCESS SHARE its reads already take; it takes no row locks on the sources because it never writes them. The only writes to a table that already has rows are the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE branches on workforce_legacy_links and workforce_quarantine, which are brand-new tables in this same transaction. The `revoke all` + `grant` block takes catalog locks only. Safe to apply BEFORE any consumer change: three new relations and two new views that nothing reads. THE ONE RISK IS VOLUME, NOT LOCKING: the backfill is unbounded in the number of distinct free-text department values, so the statement timeout is raised to 60s here from the 15s used elsewhere, and preflight.rowCountQueries carries the two counts the operator needs to decide whether to raise it further or to run the backfill on a target with a smaller free-text population first.
execution.idempotency: Deterministic and repeatable. `create table if not exists`, `create index if not exists`, `create or replace` for both trigger functions and both views, `drop trigger if exists` before each `create trigger`, `drop policy if exists` + `create policy` with a final name for each of the nine policies, `revoke all` + narrow `grant` (a reset, so a re-run also repairs a target where a default-privileges sweep granted the ledger to everyone), and every backfill statement guarded by `on conflict ... do update ... where <is distinct from>` or `on conflict do nothing`. Verified by applying the file THREE times in the harness over the same legacy rows: no error, and the link and quarantine counts identical after the second and third apply. The harness's own stage 4 asserts the counts are unchanged rather than asserting idempotency, so a change would be measured.

quarantine.strategy: This migration IS the quarantine. The strategy is WFC-003 §4's, applied as schema: fail-closed and TERMINAL until a human or an explicit reconciliation resolves it, with a code constrained to WFC-003's eleven and a resolution that requires resolved_at, resolved_by AND a note of at least three characters (a check constraint, so a quarantine cannot be cleared by writing one column). No row is ever auto-resolved: the ON CONFLICT branches only refresh `last_observed_at` and `observation_count` on rows that are still `resolved_at IS NULL`, so a resolved record is not silently reopened by the next backfill. `workforce_reconciliation_audit` counts links by state, quarantined open and resolved, and an `open_by_code` map so a reviewer can see WHICH ambiguity is accumulating rather than only that some ambiguity is - with COALESCE, because a subquery returning no rows yields NULL and NULL is exactly the signal CP-098 forbids treating as a zero. There is no partial-application state: one transaction, and the post-condition RAISEs if the asserted state is unreachable. THE BACKFILL IS ITSELF A BATCH and its size is the operator's to size: see preflight and the resumeStrategy's volume risk.
quarantine.lockBudget: The five sources are read with a full scan each (they are small operational tables and no index on `department`, `vendor_name` or `org_id IS NULL` is added to a pre-existing table, because adding one would be a change to a relation this file does not own). The quarantine's own indexes - open-code, open-org, and the subject key - are on new tables and cover every lookup the policies and the audit view perform. The ledger's read paths are served by workforce_operational_status_events_dept_effective_idx (department_id, effective_at desc, recorded_at desc), which is a prefix match for the `not exists (supersedes)` current-value query's grouping, and by _membership_idx / _person_idx for a single worker's history.

constraints: workforce_legacy_links_subject_present CHECK (subject_id IS NOT NULL OR subject_key IS NOT NULL) - a link row that identifies nothing is a reconciliation row about an unknown subject, which this table must not be able to hold. Needed because several sources key on a value rather than a uuid.

workforce_legacy_links_state_code_agreement CHECK - an unresolved row MUST carry a WORKFORCE_QUARANTINE_CODES code and a linked row must NOT. This is the assertion that makes 'unresolved records remain explicitly reviewable' structural rather than conventional. The post-condition re-checks it post-hoc, which is what catches a constraint that was silently validated away.

workforce_legacy_links_target_agreement CHECK - a linked row must actually name a target. A row that claims to be linked with no target_id is the exact shape of a reconciliation that was never performed.
workforce_legacy_links_quarantine_code_check CHECK over all eleven WFC-003 codes - so a code the application can emit can always be stored, and a code it cannot emit cannot.

workforce_quarantine_resolution_complete CHECK - all three of resolved_at, resolved_by and a note of at least three characters, or none of them. A quarantine cleared with no note is indistinguishable from one that was never really examined.

workforce_operational_status_events_department_fkey FOREIGN KEY (department_id, org_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT - the history-preservation guarantee. MEASURED: a DELETE of a department that has status history is refused 23503, so a department is deactivated rather than deleted and CP-095's append-only correction path cannot be defeated by a cascade.

workforce_operational_status_events_membership_fkey FOREIGN KEY (membership_id, department_id, person_user_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT - a THREE-column composite. A status event therefore cannot name a person who is not in the named department, and cannot name a membership from another department. MEASURED 23503 for an event in org B naming a membership in org A. This is the identity half of CP-095: the ledger is about a real (department, person) membership or it is not writable, and the guarantee is a constraint rather than an application check.

workforce_operational_status_events_supersedes_same_scope_fkey FOREIGN KEY (supersedes_event_id, org_id, department_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT - a correction is bounded to its own tenant and department. MEASURED 23503 for a cross-scope supersede. Combined with the current-value view treating any event that some other event supersedes as history, a correction can neither silently become the answer nor be orphaned.
workforce_operational_status_events_id_org_dept_key UNIQUE (id, org_id, department_id) - the composite target for the supersedes foreign key.
workforce_operational_status_events_no_self_supersede CHECK (supersedes_event_id IS NULL OR supersedes_event_id <> id) - an event that supersedes itself is not a correction.

workforce_operational_status_events_reason_required CHECK - the row-local rule described in the assumptions. It is a CHECK and not a trigger because it needs only columns of its own row, so it cannot be bypassed by a writer that forgets to validate in the application, and it costs nothing at plan time.

The nine policies ARE the authorization boundary and each arm's reason is on the policy's own COMMENT. Links and quarantine: SELECT admits org-wide workforce.view OR manage; INSERT and UPDATE require org-wide workforce.manage on both clauses; no DELETE policy and no DELETE privilege for any role. The ledger: SELECT admits org-wide view OR manage OR managing THIS department, OR the worker's own history - the last arm additionally requiring ACTIVE org membership through is_org_member, so a REVOKED member loses even their own status history rather than retaining it, and there is deliberately no read path for a department member who is not its manager. Ledger INSERT requires department-management authority AND workforce.view on the row's organization, with the department-scoped arm evaluated against the row's OWN department_id so a manager of department A cannot write into department B.
indexes: workforce_legacy_links_subject_key_uidx UNIQUE (subject_table, coalesce(subject_id::text, subject_key)) - one row per legacy subject, and the COALESCE is what makes it TOTAL across a uuid-keyed and a value-keyed source. Deliberately NOT partial, and the contract test lists it in a separate `wfc_total_index` set for that reason: a resolved link must not be replaced by a fresh unresolved one on the next backfill. The first revision of the contract test wrongly required partiality here and reported both reconciliation indexes as violations - the indexes were right and the check was wrong.
workforce_legacy_links_org_state_idx (org_id, link_state) WHERE org_id IS NOT NULL - the reconciliation worklist for one organization, and the access pattern the RLS policy's own conjuncts produce.

workforce_legacy_links_target_idx (target_kind, target_id) WHERE target_id IS NOT NULL and _code_idx (quarantine_code) WHERE quarantine_code IS NOT NULL - reverse lookup from a canonical entity to the legacy rows that pointed at it, and grouping a review by code.
workforce_quarantine_subject_uidx UNIQUE (subject_table, code, coalesce(subject_id::text, subject_key)) - one open-or-resolved quarantine per subject per code, total for the same reason as above.

workforce_quarantine_open_code_idx (code) WHERE resolved_at IS NULL and _open_org_idx (org_id, code) WHERE resolved_at IS NULL AND org_id IS NOT NULL - the open worklist, both directions, partial on `resolved_at IS NULL` so the index shrinks as work is done.

workforce_operational_status_events_dept_effective_idx (department_id, effective_at desc, recorded_at desc) - the current-value view's grouping and ordering, a prefix match, so resolving the present from the history is an index-only scan of at most a handful of rows per worker.
workforce_operational_status_events_org_effective_idx (org_id, effective_at desc) - the organization-level timeline WFC-005's read model needs.

workforce_operational_status_events_person_idx (person_user_id, effective_at desc) and _membership_idx (membership_id, effective_at desc) - a single worker's history and a single membership's history, the two reads the self-SELECT arm and the audit view perform.

workforce_operational_status_events_supersedes_idx (supersedes_event_id) WHERE supersedes_event_id IS NOT NULL - the `not exists (supersedes)` lookup in the current-value view, which is the one query that must not degrade into a sequential scan as history accumulates.
constraintsAndIndexes.validationPlan: supabase/tests/wfc004_workforce_departments_contract.sql returns violation rows only, plus one summary row `WFC-004 workforce departments|t|0` computed from the same materialised violation set it prints. recovery.rollback: DROP VIEW IF EXISTS public.workforce_operational_status_current; DROP VIEW IF EXISTS public.workforce_reconciliation_audit; DROP TABLE public.workforce_operational_status_events; DROP TABLE public.workforce_quarantine; DROP TABLE public.workforce_legacy_links; - issued as a later forward migration, never as an edit to this file. The backfilled rows go with the tables, and that is the correct rollback for THIS file: they are records ABOUT legacy data, derived from it, and re-running the file reproduces them. Rolling back does NOT lose any pre-existing row, because this file reads the five sources and never writes them. If a later migration has pointed something at these relations, the drops will be blocked by foreign keys and the correct response is a forward fix.
recovery.forwardFix: Any correction is a new additive migration with a higher version. Four shapes are worth naming. (1) A permission change is a DROP+CREATE POLICY, and the post-condition's conjunct and anon/PUBLIC checks fail the apply if the new predicate is wrong. (2) A change to the ledger's immutability is NOT a forward fix in the usual sense: the trigger is the control and a migration that drops it would fail the post-condition's required-trigger check, which is the intended behaviour. (3) A change to the status vocabulary is a CHECK constraint change, and because the vocabulary is transcribed from the exec plan's 'Manager status vocabulary', a migration that widens it must also update the plan or it will have made the schema and the contract disagree. (4) A change to the quarantine vocabulary must add the code to WFC-003's `WORKFORCE_QUARANTINE_CODES` FIRST - the CHECK constraint is the copy, and a code the application can emit but the constraint rejects is an insert failure at runtime, not a lint error. Note that a forward fix CANNOT accidentally inherit a name the 20260823210000 sweep exempts, because every policy here is named wfc004_* and matches none of the six exemption patterns.

labelledProbes: PROBE 1, EXPECTED 42501 or `permission denied`, run as the table owner or as service_role: UPDATE and DELETE on workforce_operational_status_events. Then run it again with `grant update ... to service_role` issued by hand first - it must STILL be refused, by the trigger. Three mechanisms, and removing any one still leaves the history unrewritable.

PROBE 2, EXPECTED 42501: an INSERT whose recorded_by is not the acting user, with a JWT present. The actor trigger must refuse it; a row whose actor is a third party is a ledger that cannot be used as evidence.

PROBE 3, EXPECTED 23514 twice: an `absent` event with no reason, and an ordinary `working` event with effective_at three days in the past and no reason. Then EXPECTED success for the same two WITH a reason, and for a present-tense `released` with no reason. A reason requirement that is too broad is as much a defect as one that is missing, and it is measured in both directions.
PROBE 4, EXPECTED 23503: a status event in organization B with supersedes_event_id pointing at an event in organization A. A correction must stay inside its own scope.
PROBE 5, EXPECTED 23503: `DELETE FROM workforce_departments WHERE id = <a department with status history>`. A department is deactivated, never deleted, once it has history.

PROBE 6, EXPECTED 42501: a worker with only a secondary membership inserting a status event naming their own membership. A worker cannot write a manager state at all, which is the structural half of CP-095.

PROBE 7, EXPECTED success: an organization administrator inserting an event, then reading it back. The ledger must be WRITABLE by its intended caller or it is theatre; a ledger nothing can write to is a plausible-zero generator of the CP-110 kind.

PROBE 8, EXPECTED FEWER rows than exist: an org administrator's `select count(*) from workforce_legacy_links` versus the table's true count. Rows whose subject has no established organization are invisible by design and that is CORRECT. An operator seeing a shortfall should read workforce_reconciliation_audit, not widen the policy.

PROBE 9, EXPECTED the counts unchanged: run the eleven backfill statements again (or re-apply this file) and compare `select count(*) from workforce_legacy_links` and `from workforce_quarantine` before and after. Acceptance criterion 4 is a count, not an intention, and this is how it is checked on a real target.

exceptions.rationale: Two statements insert one row per chain-absent reader relation from a literal VALUES list rather than from a table, so they carry no WHERE clause. Their source IS their scope: six lines of this migration, each naming a relation, its reader sites and its recorded disposition as the evidence payload. There is no relation being read, so there is no filter that could be absent. Every other backfill statement in this file reads a real table and carries a WHERE, and the marker distinguishes the two cases rather than excusing the rule.
exceptions.issue: check-migration-validation's scoped-insert-select rule cannot distinguish an INSERT...SELECT over a literal VALUES list from an unbounded backfill. Both look identical to the rule, and the honest response is to mark the reviewed case and carry the evidence in the manifest rather than to add a WHERE clause that does not mean anything.
exceptions.evidence: executed:supabase/tests/wfc004_workforce_departments.harness.sh stage 4 asserts the six vendor_table_unproven quarantine rows exist by name, that every link row carries non-empty evidence, and that a third apply leaves the link and quarantine counts unchanged (14 and 13 respectively on the harness fixture).
exceptions.renewalRationale: Scoped to the two literal-VALUES table-level observation statements. It expires rather than being made permanent because the rule it excuses is a proxy: once the validator can distinguish an INSERT...SELECT over a literal VALUES list from an unbounded table backfill, this exception should be withdrawn and the rule applied on its own terms. Renewal is the vendor-domain owner's decision, not this lane's - it is the column contract for org_contracts and contract_signature_envelopes that would remove the ambiguity, and WFC-003 decides the vendors/org_vendors merge.
